claims.text: Integrating CALPHAD, targeted high-throughput AIMD, modulation DSC, and high-speed imaging enables accurate and efficient determination of melting and liquid-phase properties in high-entropy alloys.
The proposed method can determine melting temperature, enthalpy of fusion, entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties.
The starting samples are solid-state high-entropy alloys with well-defined equilibrium compositions.
The hybrid technique couples CALPHAD free-energy parameterization with AIMD simulations and cross-validates them using modulation DSC and high-speed imaging.
The method is intended to operate under controlled atmospheric pressure and temperature conditions across compositions typical of high-entropy alloys.
Atomic structural rearrangements and volumetric changes at the melting boundary are detectable both computationally and experimentally.
CALPHAD provides a predictive free-energy landscape for high-entropy-alloy melting.
AIMD captures dynamic atomic rearrangements during melting and can refine the CALPHAD description.
Combining CALPHAD and AIMD with DSC and imaging measurements permits identification of melting onset and associated thermodynamic properties.
Integrated-model predictions will agree with experimental melting-property benchmarks within approximately 5–10%.
DSC or AIMD used in isolation typically deviates by 10–15% from precise experimental measurements.
The approach is expected to remain valid within compositional and microstructural regimes typical of high-entropy alloys.
Accuracy may diminish for extreme alloy compositions or systems with significant non-equilibrium features.
AIMD may not scale efficiently over very large compositional spaces.
Computational cost may limit the practical breadth of the proposed method.
Statistically significant prediction errors greater than 10% across the tested alloys would falsify the proposed reliability claim.
